title: Incident taxonomy v1: draft + socialization + review signoff
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Reliability Program: Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping
description:
## Context
We need a v1 incident taxonomy that on-call can apply *during an incident* (fast, low ambiguity) and that also supports reporting (bounded categories, stable over time, low-cardinality labels).

This ticket owns the **v1 proposal** (types/subtypes + definitions + decision tree) and the **review/signoff workflow** across SRE/Platform/Infra/Runtime/Observability/Support.

## Goals
- Produce a bounded v1 taxonomy (target: ~10–15 top-level types; each with a small set of subtypes where needed).
- Provide clear definitions + inclusion/exclusion criteria to reduce “misc/other”.
- Include a quick decision tree usable by incident commander within ~2 minutes.
- Socialize and reach cross-team signoff so we can enforce taxonomy as required fields in incident-bot.

## Inputs / data sources
- Top incidents analysis (last 2 quarters) + clustering notes (Drive)
- Recent incident-bot history + postmortems (last 90 days)
- Support escalations (Dedicated/Private)

## Draft taxonomy (v1 proposal)
**Top-level incident types (proposed):**
1) Availability / 5xx
2) Latency regression
3) Streaming disconnects / degraded streaming
4) Routing / fallback misbehavior
5) Capacity / fleet shortage
6) Control plane outage / degraded control plane
7) Auth / RBAC failures
8) Telemetry blind spot (metrics/logging/tracing gaps impacting detection/triage)
9) Private deployment connectivity / config issues
10) Rollout regression (model/runtime/control plane change introducing reliability regression)

**Notes on boundaries:**
- If customer requests are failing (5xx/timeouts), classify based on *primary customer symptom*, then tag contributing systems separately in postmortem.
- Capacity vs routing: capacity when demand > supply (GPU saturation/provisioning lag/region constraints); routing when policy/health/fallback logic misroutes or fails to degrade gracefully.
- Telemetry blind spot is used only when inability to observe materially increases MTTA/MTTR or causes incorrect mitigation; not for “dashboards are annoying”.

## Deliverables
- Confluence page: taxonomy v1 definitions + examples + inclusion/exclusion + decision tree
- A short “how to classify” section for on-call playbooks (IC + primary on-call)
- Reviewer list + signoff recorded (comment/email thread)
- Handoff to ownership mapping + SLA matrix workstream

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Bounded set of top-level types (<= 15) with stable names and minimal overlap
- [x] Each type has: definition, inclusion criteria, exclusion criteria, at least 2 examples
- [x] Decision tree covers the top 80–90% of incidents with <10 steps
- [x] Reviewers from SRE, Platform (Control Plane + Routing), Infra/Fleet, Runtime, Observability, Support sign off
- [x] Observability approves taxonomy naming for metric labeling (cardinality guardrails)

## Reviewers / stakeholders
- SRE: Rafael Mendes (lead), Sean Gallagher (sponsor)
- Observability: Allison Grant
- Platform (control plane / owner mapping): Ethan Park
- Routing: Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon
- Fleet/capacity: Vanessa Ortiz, Harish Reddy
- Runtime: Sofia Ivanova, Noah Patel
- Support/CS validation: Dev Patel, Owen Phillips

## Workshop plan
- Pre-read: taxonomy draft + top-incident analysis
- 60 min working session:
  - Agree top-level types + naming
  - Resolve boundary disputes (capacity vs routing; latency vs rollout regression; streaming vs client)
  - Identify any missing type that would create a large “unknown” bucket
- 30 min async follow-up: integrate edits + publish v1 + announce rollout timeline

## Related links
- Drive: Top incidents analysis (last 2 quarters): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/top-incidents-analysis-last-2-quarters
- Drive: Decision tree draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/incident-type-decision-tree-draft
- Confluence (draft): Incident taxonomy v1 definitions: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGSRE/Incident+taxonomy+v1+definitions
- Linear follow-ups:
  - ENG-4822 (incident-bot required fields)
  - ENG-4826 (metric labels + cardinality)
  - ENG-4827 (90-day backfill)

## Open questions to resolve in review
1) Do we keep “Rollout regression” as a distinct top-level type, or treat as a subtype under Availability/Latency/etc.?
2) Where do we put “quota/throttling” (429s)? Under Availability vs Capacity vs Auth?
3) Private connectivity: split DNS/TLS vs control plane connectivity vs customer-side misconfig?
4) Do we need a dedicated “External dependency / cloud provider” flag vs treating as contributing factor?

## Out of scope
- Deep root cause frameworks (belongs in postmortems)
- Multi-dimensional tagging beyond one primary type + optional contributing systems
comments: 2025-12-03 (Mei Lin): Pulled last 2 quarters incident list from incident-bot export + postmortems. Biggest clusters by symptom: 5xx/overload, p95 latency regressions, streaming resets, and control plane write failures. Drafting top-level categories with the constraint that they must be label-safe for metrics.

2025-12-05 (Rafael Mendes): Shared v0.2 taxonomy draft in #eng-sre and requested feedback on boundaries (capacity vs routing; telemetry vs latency false positives). Added acceptance criteria explicitly limiting top-level types to <= 15.

2025-12-06 (Allison Grant): +1 on keeping v1 small. Please avoid “per-service” categories. For metrics: prefer a fixed allowlist with an explicit `unknown/unclassified` bucket; no freeform strings. Also ensure subtypes are capped and documented.

2025-12-07 (Sofia Ivanova): Runtime-specific failure modes are often reported as latency/5xx. We should include runtime subtypes under Latency regression and Availability/5xx rather than a separate top-level “Runtime”. Example subtypes: scheduler stalls, KV cache thrash, OOM, quantization/kernels regression. I’ll provide concrete examples + what signals to look at.

2025-12-09 (Vanessa Ortiz): Capacity/fleet shortage needs to cover both regional GPU saturation and provisioning lag (including autoscaler misconfig). Routing can own “fallback doesn’t happen” but Fleet should own “no capacity to fall back to”. Suggest decision tree question: 'Is there insufficient healthy capacity in region(s) for the requested model?'

2025-12-10 (Dev Patel): Support needs a clear rule for 429s on Dedicated: sometimes quota, sometimes saturation. Proposal: if enforcement is expected/intentional -> 'Quota/Rate limiting' subtype; if unexpected and driven by saturation -> 'Capacity saturation' subtype. We can keep both under Availability/5xx + 4xx (or create an 'Overload & throttling' top-level).

2025-12-11 (Rafael Mendes): Scheduling workshop for 2025-12-12. Agenda: finalize top-level names; decide on Rollout regression placement; settle 429s classification. Goal is to publish v1 by EOW to unblock ENG-4822.

2025-12-12 (Workshop notes summary - Mei Lin): Decisions: (1) Keep 'Rollout regression' as a subtype (not top-level) to preserve single-axis primary symptom classification; (2) Add explicit 'Throttling / 429s' under Availability/5xx with subtypes 'intentional quota' vs 'unintended saturation'; (3) Telemetry blind spot stays as top-level but with strict inclusion criteria (must materially impact MTTA/MTTR). Action: Mei to update decision tree and add at least 2 examples per type by 12/13.

2025-12-13 (Sean Gallagher): Approved v1 scope and rollout plan. Key ask: ensure 'unknown' has an explicit process (temporary classification + follow-up within 24h). Also track classification compliance as a program metric.

2025-12-13 (Rafael Mendes): Published v1 draft to Confluence and started async signoff thread (SRE/Platform/Infra/Runtime/Obs/Support). Marking this ticket as done once all reviewer approvals are in and links are stable for ENG-4822 implementation.

2026-01-10 (Mei Lin): Final reviewer approvals captured (Routing + Fleet ownership boundaries accepted; Observability approved allowlist naming). Linked final Confluence page in ticket. Follow-up work continues in ENG-4827 (backfill) to validate category distribution and tighten examples for v1.1.
